identity.title: ALMA observations of RCW 120 Fragmentation at 0.01 pc scale&star

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using ALMA 3 mm continuum observations towards the densest and most massive millimetric condensation (Condensation 1) of RCW 120, we used the getimages and getsources algorithms to extract the sources detected with ALMA

evidence.quote: located 0.5$^\circ$ above the Galactic Plane at a distance of 1.3 kpc

question.value: How do the most massive Herschel cores in Condensation 1 of the RCW 120 H II region fragment down to 0.01 pc, and can high-mass stars form there?

evidence.quote: We want to study the fragmentation process down to the 0.01 pc scale in the most massive condensation (1700 $M_{\odot}$) observed at the south-western edge of the H  region RCW 120
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00314.S.
We used a continuum bandwith of 2.227 GHz in Band 3
The spectral bands were centered on 93.17, 91.98, 104.02 and 102.5 GHz
allowing the observations of N$_2$H$^+$, CH$_3$CN, SO$_2$ transition lines and 3 mm continuum emission
allowing the observations of N$_2$H$^+$, CH$_3$CN, SO$_2$ transition lines and 3 mm continuum emission
allowing the observations of N$_2$H$^+$, CH$_3$CN, SO$_2$ transition lines and 3 mm continuum emission
using 38 of the 40 12 m ALMA antennas in nominal configuration C40-3 with baselines ranging from 15 m to 459 m
synthesized beam of 1.7$''$$\times$1.5$''$ (0.01 pc at a distance of 1.3 kpc)
The largest recoverable angular scale for these observations is 14$''$.
The total observing time was 27.8 minutes

findings_qualitative.value: CH3CN and SO2 emission toward Fragment 1 suggests a probable UC HII region

evidence.quote: CH$_3$CN and SO$_2$ emission are observed towards the main fragment in the most massive core arguing for the presence of an UCH  region in the PDR.

claims.hypothesis: Do the cores fragment as predicted by thermal Jeans fragmentation?
claims.experiment: Compare 18 ALMA fragments with thermal Jeans masses of Herschel cores
claims.result: Fewer fragments than expected; three cores with none
claims.finding: Fragmentation inconsistent with ideal gravitational fragmentation; turbulence or magnetic fields needed

evidence.quote: the observed fragmentation is inconsistent with ideal gravitational fragmentation and other ingredients such as turbulence or magnetic fields should be added

claims.hypothesis: Is Condensation 1 favourable for high-mass star formation?
claims.result: Fragments up to 32 Msun; line emission toward Fragment 1
claims.finding: Favourable place with probable UCHII region

evidence.quote: Condensation 1 of RCW 120 is a favourable place for the formation of high-mass stars.

limitations_admitted.value: Only 20% of emission recovered; extended emission filtered

evidence.quote: while the emission above 14$''$  is filtered and lost

referee_caveats_inferred: Fragment masses assume host-core temperature, uncertain by factor 2 plus opacity
Short single-pointing observation; fragment completeness not tested
Jeans comparison uses assumed 0.1 pc scale
